newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish zloty pushed down by strong dlr, O/N flat.
newsitem.headline: Polish zloty pushed down by strong dlr, O/N flat.

text.p: The Polish zloty inched down against the basket in slow early trade dominated by dollar/mark movements on world markets amid few domestic client orders to spice up trade, dealers said.

"The market is quietly tracking dollar/mark moves this morning and for as long as the dollar holds above 1.48 marks, the zloty is likely to stay weak," said Malgorzata Pantow, forex dealer at Pekao SA.
At 0830 GMT the zloty was at 1.68/1.62 percent from the trading band centre, weaker than 1.78/1.71 percent from parity at 0703 GMT and Wednesday's close at 1.75/1.70 percent.
The zloty was at 2.7475/90 to the dollar, down from 2.7435/65 at 0703 GMT and flat from Wednesday's 2.7480/90.
It was at 1.8550/60 to the mark, just down from opening's 1.8540/60 and weaker than Wednesday's 1.8496/07.
On the money market overnight rates held at opening levels during morning trade as Thursday's 580 million zloty net outflow from the system kept the market short-of-cash.

O/N rates were at 19.00/19.45 percent, up from Wednesday's close at 18.80/19.30 percent and tomorrow/next rates opened at 19.1/19.6 percent, nearly unchanged from 19.2/19.7 percent on Wednesday and above the main 14-day reverse repo rate of 19.05.
Earlier today the central bank released its preliminatry broad money data, which showed that money supply rose 1.7 percent in August a 2.3 percent rise in July.
Broad money supply grew 16.7 percent in the January-August period against 20.9 percent in the same period of last year.
The bank also said net currency reserves, held by the whole banking system, grew $80.6 million in August 1-20 to $22.04 billion and were $1.6 billion higher than in December 1995.
